prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1430; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a low-speed collision in a shopping center parking lot. The claimant said a vehicle backed into their driver's side while they were stopped in a parking space, and they went to hospital afterward with head pain and dizziness.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. They are handling the claim themselves and have not retained a lawyer. They gave the same account of the impact as in the first report and said they were in the driver's seat when it happened.

Entry 3: Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the vehicles touched while the claimant's car was parked and that they exchanged information on the spot. Their description of the contact matches what the claimant reported.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant and the scene photos from the store's security team. The paint transfer and bumper damage are consistent with a rear-quarter impact at low speed.

Entry 5: Police report received. The responding officer recorded the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and noted two independent witnesses who saw the contact. Both witnesses' statements agree with the claimant's account.

Entry 6: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The visible damage is largely in line with the impact described, and I found nothing suggesting earlier body work on the affected panels.

Entry 7: Medical records received. The diagnosis is a concussion, which fits the nature and force of the collision. The treatment followed a typical course, with follow-up visits tapering as symptoms improved.

Entry 8: A neighbor contacted our office and stated the car showed damage a few weeks before the reported date. I have asked for a written statement and any photos or repair records that would show the vehicle's condition at that earlier time.

Entry 9: Checked the policy. The driver involved is listed on it. No prior injury to the same area of the head or neck appears in the medical history provided, and I am continuing to review the neighbor's information before a decision on the claim.
